text.p: Morgan Stanley Asia said it has downgraded Yizheng Chemical Fibre Ltd to neutral from outperform, due to the failure of forecast margin expansion to materialise, and cut earnings forecasts for 1996-98.
"The problem we see is that the margin pickup in 1997 and 1998 may not be as exciting as we previously perceived," said analyst Edward Yu in a report released on Wednesday.
The company was cutting its 1996 earnings per share estimates by 58 percent to HK$0.05 from HK$0.12 for 1996, the report said.
Yu also lowered 1997 and 1998 estimates by 73 percent and 42 percent to HK$0.06 and HK$0.14, primarily because of slower than forecast margin expansion.

"We never thought prices would take off but margin expansion would have helped Yizheng's earnings from the second half of 1996 until the supply/demand balance for end-products (in polyester industry) improved sometime in 1998," he said.
"However local PTA (purified terephthalic acid) costs have held firm and internal PTA costs were higher than expected in the second half of 1996," the report said.
The broker also lowered its 1996 dividend estimate to HK$0.03 from HK$0.06 and warned that a equity issue might be needed to help fund the company's large expansion programme.
"Our new 12-month price target is HK$1.95, which is based on an 85 percent relative market multiple to our forecast of Yizheng's normalised earnings of HK$0.19," the report said.
Yizheng closed HK$0.01 lower at HK$1.640 on Wednesday.
